settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: checkEnableEvalExpression explicitly rejects eval expressions when not enabled (OgnlUtil.java lines 356-360).
Static method access is denied by default via checkStaticMethodAccess unless allowStaticMethodAccess is true (SecurityMemberAccess.java lines 94-101).
createDefaultContext propagates excludedClasses and excludedPackageNamePatterns into SecurityMemberAccess (OgnlUtil.java lines 583-587).
SecurityMemberAccess.isClassExcluded blocks Object.class and configured excluded classes and their subtypes (lines 121-131), and isPackageExcluded blocks matching packages (lines 112-119).
candidates.description: OgnlUtil.setValue/getValue/copy compile and evaluate OGNL expressions derived from property names supplied through the request-driven parameters map. This is the central OGNL ingestion point in the framework. Security depends on three injected controls: excludedClasses, excludedPackageNamePatterns, and the eval-expression flag. In the reviewed snapshot these controls are wired: setExcludedClasses loads configured class names and throws ConfigurationException on unknown names (lines 99-109); setExcludedPackageName enables allowStaticMethodAccess and other settings are propagated into SecurityMemberAccess in createDefaultContext (lines 577-588). checkEnableEvalExpression throws unless eval-expressions were explicitly enabled (lines 356-360), and the setter logs a security warning when they are enabled (lines 91-97). Because the effective security posture depends entirely on the deployed configuration values (XWorkConstants.OGNL_EXCLUDED_CLASSES, ...PACKAGE_NAME_PATTERNS, ALLOW_STATIC_METHOD_ACCESS), a deployment that omits or narrows these lists could allow access to classes/members the defaults intend to block. This is a candidate concern, not a confirmed vulnerability.
missing_evidence: The effective default values of XWorkConstants.OGNL_EXCLUDED_CLASSES and OGNL_EXCLUDED_PACKAGE_NAME_PATTERNS in DefaultProperties/default config were not read in this review.
No end-to-end request-handling test or runtime trace proving an attacker-controlled expression reaches Ognl.setValue without a block was inspected.
Whether a specific excluded-class list is sufficient to block the well-known gadget chains is a configuration question not answerable from the single reviewed file.
preconditions: Application routes attacker-controllable parameter names into the ParametersInterceptor/OGNL setValue path (default Struts2 behavior).
Deployment configuration fails to set OGNL excluded classes/package patterns to the framework-recommended values, or sets allowStaticMethodAccess=true.
The eval-expression feature must be enabled for %{...} eval-style parameter names to be honored (otherwise those are rejected).
candidates.title: OGNL expression evaluation via OgnlUtil with excluded-class / package-pattern guardrails present

counter_evidence: MAX_RECURSION is a constant 1 (TextParseUtil.java line 40), bounding nested evaluation.
OgnlTextParser explicitly breaks when loopCount > maxLoopCount, with an inline comment that this prevents infinite loop / recursive expression evaluation (OgnlTextParser.java lines 27-29).
candidates.description: TextParseUtil.translateVariables resolves ${...} and %{...} occurrences by invoking the injected TextParser (OgnlTextParser) with a max loop count. MAX_RECURSION is set to 1 (line 40), and OgnlTextParser.evaluate breaks out of the loop when loopCount exceeds maxLoopCount (lines 27-29). translateVariables is called from many result/view components (e.g., StrutsResultSupport, HttpHeaderResult, XSLTResult, ActionChainResult) whose input strings can incorporate request-influenced values. With the recursion cap of 1, a second-level recursive evaluation of a value that itself contains ${...} is not performed by this path, which limits double-evaluation amplification. This is recorded as a design observation; the cap value is the mitigating factor, so it is not asserted as a finding of vulnerability.
missing_evidence: No inspection of every translateVariables call site was completed to confirm none pass a larger maxLoopCount.
No runtime test showing whether nested ${} inside a resolved value is or is not re-evaluated on a live request.
preconditions: A component calls TextParseUtil.translateVariables on a string that contains attacker-influenced content with expression syntax.
The attacker attempts to chain evaluation so that the resolved value is itself treated as an expression.
candidates.title: Recursive OGNL evaluation limited to MAX_RECURSION=1 in TextParseUtil/OgnlTextParser
